input: Read /data/export.tsv which is tab-separated with columns: id, last_name, first_name, email, department. Convert it to /data/import.csv (comma-separated) with columns reordered to: email, first_name, last_name, department (dropping the id column). Include a header row. Print the result.

transcript.final_response:
I converted the file and saved it as `/data/import.csv`. Here's the result:

```
email,first_name,last_name,department
alice@co.com,Alice,Smith,Eng
bob@co.com,Bob,Jones,Sales
carol@co.com,Carol,Davis,Eng
dave@co.com,Dave,Wilson,HR
```

The header row plus all 4 records are there. The columns are reordered to email, first_name, last_name, department, and the id column is gone.

None of the values had commas or quotes in them, so nothing needed quoting. The script would still add quotes correctly if you run it on data that does have them.
tool_calls:
awk -F'\t' 'function q(s){ if (s ~ /[",\r\n]/) { gsub(/"/,"\"\"",s); s="\"" s "\"" } return s }
{ sub(/\r$/,""); print q($4) "," q($3) "," q($2) "," q($5) }' /data/export.tsv > /data/import.csv; cat /data/import.csv
